Timeline::set_minute¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline Timeline::set_minute(int minute) const

Replace One Clock Field¶

set_minute() replaces the local minute of every defined timestamp with a value in [0, 59]. It returns a new Timeline; the receiver is not modified. Year, month, day, hour, second, fractional nanoseconds, timezone, rank, and shape are retained.

Use it when the minute number is the desired invariant, such as moving a set of local appointment times to quarter past their existing hours. It is not a minute offset: set_minute(15) means HH:15, not “15 minutes later.”

Example: Set Every Lane To Quarter Past¶

const auto t = pluss::timeline::make({
    {"2024-01-15T23:58:59.123456789Z", "2024-06-20T04:05:06.000000004Z"},
    {"2024-09-28T12:30:45.900000000Z", "2024-12-01T00:00:00.000000001Z"},
});

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(t.set_minute(15), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["2024-01-15T23:15:59.123456789+00:00", "2024-06-20T04:15:06.000000004+00:00"], 
  ["2024-09-28T12:15:45.900000000+00:00", "2024-12-01T00:15:00.000000001+00:00"]
]

Seconds and nanoseconds are deliberately nonzero in this example. They prove that set_minute() edits only its named field rather than rounding to minute precision.

Example: Compose A Complete Local Clock¶

const auto t = pluss::timeline::make("2024-08-19T21:47:36.250000001Z");
const auto opening = t.set_hour(9).set_minute(30).set_second(0);

std::cout << pluss::timeline::format(opening, "%FT%T.%f%z").at(0) << '\n';

Output¶

2024-08-19T09:30:00.250000001+00:00

Chaining is evaluated from left to right, and every call returns a new timeline. The fractional component remains 250000001 because none of these three methods replaces nanoseconds.

Bounds, Absence, And Timezones¶

-1 and 60 throw; there is no wrapping into the adjacent hour. Validation also occurs for empty input. NaT lanes remain NaT.

The minute is interpreted in the timeline’s current timezone. Although most timezone transitions occur on an hour boundary, the complete reconstructed local timestamp is still checked. A nonexistent local result throws, and the first occurrence is selected if the result is ambiguous.

See Also¶

  • minute: inspect the local minute.

  • set_hour: replace the enclosing hour.

  • set_second: replace seconds without losing nanoseconds.
